summary: A documented, runnable multi-rail payment adapter for agent wallets: one PaymentRail interface with a working example settling the same x402 payment on two rails - EVM/Base USDC (the status-quo distribution rail) and Nano (XNO, feeless/sub-second/self-custody). Reuses the existing Nano x402 client (feeless402 + x402nano-exact) instead of rebuilding payment logic.

target.ecosystem: Agent-wallet SDKs outside the Nano ecosystem (heath territory: Coinbase AgentKit, Crossmint, Skyfire, Payman, Nevermined and other agent-wallet SDKs)
target.audience: developers building AI agents that pay x402-priced HTTP endpoints, and the maintainers of agent-wallet SDKs deciding which settlement rails to support
target.why_missing: Every agent-wallet SDK that supports x402 today settles on EVM/Base USDC (or Solana) only - AgentKit, Crossmint, Skyfire, Payman, Nevermined all stop at stablecoin rails. None documented a Nano (XNO) rail: feeless per transfer, sub-second finality, self-custodial (no freezeable stablecoin, no per-tx gas). There is no runnable, documented multi-rail adapter that shows an agent settling the SAME payment on USDC-on-EVM and XNO behind one interface. This example proves the shape so a first contact to any of those SDKs can cite a working, tested artifact instead of a claim.

novelty: No runnable multi-rail agent-payment adapter exists anywhere for wallet SDKs (verified: AgentKit, Crossmint, Skyfire, Nevermined, Payman each ship single-rail USDC; no repo shows USDC-on-EVM AND XNO behind one interface). This is a thin documented interface with two concrete rails - it rebuilds no payment logic on either rail, wrapping the MIT fee-free x402 Nano client for the XNO side and a minimal USDC stub for the EVM side to prove dispatch - and ships a tested runnable example that an agent-wallet maintainer can check and extend to their SDK.
